test_scope: Blinded asynchronous table-read of canonical prepared-answer transcripts. No ending seen, no live improvisation, human recall, handwriting or physical packet handling tested.
experience: Fair and satisfying elimination puzzle. I changed from Artie after motive to Hugh after opportunity to Elon after method; the final evidence defeated my suspicions without requiring arbitrary trust in guest denials.
fun: Moderate: the grievances and puns provide character, but the final solve is a three-column intersection with little interpretive uncertainty.
navigation: Round headers, STOP gates and choosing the next unanswered guest are clear in transcript and page 07. Method page 10 visibly omits the upper answer heading and innocent label in the original image.
question_matching: All prepared transcript questions matched their named groups. Broad generic group wording still works for Tess. No observed mismatch between question and answer.
repetition: Opportunity repeatedly uses 'I went into the Donor Salon' and every method answer repeats 'That was what the materials desk issued me.' This aids comparisons but makes sixteen successive answers feel mechanical. Different motive voices were more enjoyable.
sixteen_present_vs_thirty_listed: Thirty listed names create irrelevant scanning for a sixteen-person table. 'Ignore absent guests' prevents a rules block, and all sixteen attending characters answered once in each transcript. A roster or marking absent names would reduce visual search.
note_space: Page 07 has only two ruled lines, inadequate for recording sixteen times and key states. Method page 10 has no visible note area. This is a layout assessment, not a physical handwriting test.
memory_load: A human listener would need to retain three attributes for sixteen characters, names, motives and the animal. Transcript rereading made that manageable here; actual human recall was not tested. A roster grid would let deduction carry more of the difficulty.
branch_safety: ZEBRA versus twice-announced HIPPO made my innocent status unambiguous. Page 07 clearly labels both boxes. Both alternate private branches were actually present in the supplied text, and original PNGs show both branches together. This exposes my own hypothetical alternate facts, not the selected animal-to-Elon mapping. I did not use that alternative as public testimony. Wrong-box reading at a live table remains a hypothetical risk rather than an observed event.
roleplay: Tess has a strong foundation-control grievance and concrete social tasks. The optional acting instruction helps a reserved player. A contrarian can challenge records until F3-F5 explicitly shut down alternative entrances, duplicates and transfers; I accepted those constraints rather than forcing a conspiracy.
actual_disclosures: The host announced HIPPO as instructed; no suspect was named by that announcement in supplied material.
My own innocent and murderer answer boxes were visible together in text and PNGs.
The final ending remained withheld, so correct-answer confirmation was not available.
hypothetical_risks: A player could read the nearby alternate branch aloud.
A player could turn beyond STOP to Coming Clean; this did not happen in the supplied test.
Listeners without a roster grid could lose track of names or facts; no live memory failure was measured.
